summary.text: 影 means “shadow.” Its conventional analysis combines 景 as a sound element with 彡 as graphic-semantic material associated with hair ornament or decorative markings. Historical accounts describe adding 彡 to distinguish the shadow writing, though the early form sequence is not secure.

formation.text: 影 is conventionally analyzed as a phono-semantic compound: 彡 contributes graphic or semantic material, while 景 supplies a sound cue. Historical accounts describe 景 as used for “shadow” and 影 as formed by adding 彡 to that shadow-use graph, after which the written forms specialized. This supports graphic differentiation; it does not establish a progression from 景’s separate light sense or show that the shadow use began as sound-based borrowing.

components.text: 景 is the phonetic element in the conventional analysis. Modern Mandarin jǐng resembles 影 yǐng. Baxter–Sagart’s Middle Chinese and Old Chinese comparisons share rhyme and rising-tone notation but differ in initial notation. These comparisons support, but do not prove, the phonetic analysis. Historical accounts also describe 景’s use for “shadow” as a graphic counterpart to 影; they do not establish a progression from its separate light sense.

sound_limitation.text: The current and reconstructed comparisons are compatible with the traditional phonetic analysis, but do not independently prove 景’s role in the original design.

sound.text: The modern Mandarin readings are similar, though their initials differ.
Middle Chinese has the same rhyme and rising-tone notation in both readings, but different initial notation.
The Old Chinese forms share rhyme and rising-tone notation but differ in initial notation.

components.text: 彡 is the visible graphic-semantic element in the conventional account and is associated with hair ornament or decorative markings. The evidence does not establish that it literally depicts lines of shadow.

history.text: Historical accounts describe 影 as 景 with 彡 added after 景 had been used for “shadow.” This supports graphic differentiation, but does not establish that the shadow use began as a phonetic borrowing of the whole graph 景.

The attached seal-style image is a modern redraw of 景 alone. It illustrates the graph described as the base to which 彡 was added; it is neither an early form nor a dated occurrence of the complete character 影.

uncertainties.text: The earliest appearance of 影 is disputed. Scholarship favors the 405 Eastern Jin 爨寶子碑, while a Han-end commentary and a lost Zhang Heng stele have also been proposed. The claim that Ge Hong first added 彡 comes through later lexicographic reports.

No secure sequence of early forms for the complete character is established. The sound comparison supports the conventional analysis but does not prove the original design; 景’s older shadow use is documented separately from its ordinary light sense and is better supported as a lexical and graphic counterpart than as a whole-character borrowing.

senses.text: A museum catalog transcribes 影命不長 on a rubbing of the 爨寶子碑 dated 405; the date and reading are mediated by the catalog and later scholarship.
Dictionary records include image-related uses such as figures or portraits. Their first dates and a complete development from “shadow” are not established.
影 is used with the sense “photograph”; the beginning of this use and its path from “shadow” are not dated here.

limitations.text: The first dates of image, reflection, portrait, and photograph uses, and the transitions among these senses and “shadow,” remain unresolved; no semantic-development link is assigned.
The 405 attestation is supported by a cataloged rubbing and later scholarship rather than direct inspection of a contemporary original. Earlier-attestation claims remain disputed.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw created/uploaded in 2007, not an ancient artifact photograph
items.tradition: Small seal-script style, represented as 彡
items.caption: A modern redraw of 景 in a small-seal style. Historical accounts describe 影 as 景 with 彡 added to distinguish the shadow writing; this image shows 景 alone, not an early example of the complete character.
items.alt: A black seal-style graph with three long, curved strokes rising diagonally from lower left to upper right on a white background.
items.selection_reason: The image depicts 景, the graph that historical accounts identify as the base to which 彡 was added. It helps illustrate that reported graphic relationship, but cannot establish the appearance or date of an early form of 影.
items.rights: Public-domain release stated on the exact Wikimedia Commons file description page for the ancient-script representation.

limitations.text: No secure sequence of early forms for the complete character 影 is established. The selected image shows 景 alone, so it does not document a dated occurrence or early compound form of 影.
